title: 1963 AHSME Problem 17
statement:
The expression

\[ \frac{\dfrac{a}{a+y}+\dfrac{y}{a-y}} {\dfrac{y}{a+y}-\dfrac{a}{a-y}}, \]

\(a\) real, \(a\ne0,\) has the value \(-1\) for:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: all but two real values of \(y\)

solutions.text:
For \(y\ne\pm a,\) the numerator simplifies to \(\frac{a^2+y^2}{a^2-y^2}\) and the denominator to its negative. Their quotient is therefore \(-1.\) The two values \(y=a\) and \(y=-a\) are undefined.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Combine the two fractions in the numerator and denominator separately
Keep track of the excluded values \(y=\pm a\)
